title: One-sided free address twists keep the nine-call bit floor; two-sided twists pass the square-zero relaxation at seven (no new κ)
body:
## Result

Changed hypothesis for `bit-new-register-model`: free per-register **address twists** `B -> P B Q` (`P, Q` in `GL_m(Z_(2))`) between paid calls, together with free binary mixing and any number of restored dirty roles. The three-register bound (#468) and all its successors explicitly exclude these. Twisted XORs put operators in matrices over the skew group ring `F2[M_m(Q)] ⋊ G`, a nonabelian operation family on an abelian address group.

- **Theorem A (written proof, PROOF.md §3).** Suppose every frame has odd denominators and every twist reduces mod 2 to a one-sided map (`X -> P̄X` for all twists, or `X -> XQ̄` for all twists). Then any exact word needs `Σ_s rank_F2(C_s mod 2)` paid calls. For three targets invertible mod 2 that is **nine**, and the direct word attains it. One-sided twists therefore do not escape the obstruction. The proof extends #2110's square-zero map: twists are equivariant for it, and one-sidedness keeps each call rank one in a suitable flattening.
- **Proposition B (finite exact).** For two-sided twists, take `σ(B) = S B S^T`, a simultaneous swap of axes 0 and 1. An explicit **seven-call** word for `diag([I],[I],[I])` agrees with the target in the full square-zero image `M_3(Λ ⋊ G)` in all 5040 call orders. Exact skew-ring products show that **none** is a real identity. Hence no square-zero argument (Theorem A, #2110) can prove nine once two-sided twists are free. Whether they actually beat nine is **open**. No seven-call word and no sub-nine bound are claimed.

This is a scoped proof plus a finite relaxation witness, not a complete theorem for two-sided twists. There is no supplier, no native price for a relabelling, no κ change and no selected-frontier change.

## Task and overlap

- Card `bit-new-register-model` (track bit-mechanisms), priority revision 7, base `cef4b52f2a59009865bf8eabde1be3f159063703`. The scope is refined to the twist model. The reason is recorded in TASK.json.
- CLAIM: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19137646. The board was rechecked before submission and has no crossing claim.
- Distinct from #4939 and #4950 (mihir-s-05, jwr404). Those compute coordinate-SWAP costs in `M_R(F2[GL_n(F2)])`, where the address group itself is nonabelian. Here the address group stays abelian and the nonabelian part is the twist action.
- Distinct from petalas's #4909–#4919 and from the existing dirty/clean-workspace packages, which keep "no free address maps". Q8, D16, dihedral, S3, A5 and SL2(F3) packages change the address group instead.

## Test plan

- `python3.12 -B research/bit-address-twist-register-floor/verify.py`: PASS in about 6 s. Checks the direct nine-call word with 0/1 dirty helper; rejects a deleted call and a mutated frame; bounds the flattening on 240 seeded random one-sided words, with an opposite-flattening control exceeding on 108; runs all 5040 witness orders (relaxation match, 0 exact); rejects altered-target, untwisted and left-only witness controls.
- The same verifier under `python3.12 -O -B` and `python3.12 -I -W error -B`: PASS.
- `python3 scripts/research_package.py --package research/bit-address-twist-register-floor --check-only`: `PASS_PACKAGE_METADATA_AND_PINS`.
- `python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/bit-address-twist-register-floor`: `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE ... outcome=partial`.
- `python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/bit-address-twist-register-floor --check-source-history`: `PASS_RESEARCH_COMMIT_BYTES`.
- `python3.12 -W error -B -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_research_onboarding.py'`: 26 tests OK.
- Verifier mutation tests, each confirmed to FAIL: expected exact-order count 0 to 1; floor 9 to 8; flattening bound `k` to `k-1`; witness diagonal frame `E22` to `E11`.

## Open next questions

1. Can two-sided twists beat nine exactly? First step: compute the order-two term (mod the cube of the augmentation ideal) for the seven-call multiset over all `S3 × S3` twist assignments.
2. Can a native bit layout perform a per-register `PBQ` relabelling without paid work? Without that, any formal saving cannot be used.
3. Do words mixing left-only and right-only twists evade the floor? First step: an exact relaxation search with at most eight calls.
